There are {{n3}} restaurants with three Michelin stars in the world, according to the {{guideYear}} MICHELIN Guide editions. {{top3Country}} has the most, with {{top3N}}, followed by {{second3Country}} with {{second3N}}. Three stars is the highest Michelin star rating. This list was last checked {{checked}}.

Below is every 3 Michelin star restaurant, country by country, with its chef, its cuisine and what the main dinner tasting menu costs. Each name opens the restaurant’s prices on The Starred Bill, each city our full price list for that destination, and each arrow the restaurant’s page on the MICHELIN Guide. For what the stars mean, see What is a Michelin star?

3 Michelin star restaurants in Singapore, Sweden, London and the US

3 Michelin star restaurants in Singapore: the city has {{n3_singapore}}, and every 3 Michelin star Singapore restaurant is in the Singapore table above. Singapore menus are priced before the 10% service charge and 9% GST, so expect the bill to be higher than the menu price. See our Singapore page for every starred restaurant in the city.

3 Michelin star restaurants in Sweden: Sweden has {{n3_sweden}}, in the Nordic countries guide. See the Sweden table above and our Sweden page.

3 Michelin star restaurants in London and the UK: London has {{n3London}} and the UK {{n3UK}}. We list them in detail in 3 Michelin star restaurants in London and 3 Michelin star restaurants in the UK.

3 Michelin star restaurants in the US: the US has {{n3us}}, most of them in California and New York. See Michelin stars by country and state for the full count.

How to book a three-star restaurant

Tables at three-star restaurants are scarce, and the best ones are gone within minutes of release. A few habits make it much easier:

  • Know the release date. Most three-star restaurants open bookings on a fixed schedule, often on the first day of the month for the month or two ahead, or a set number of days in advance. The restaurant’s own website says when; set a reminder and book the moment the calendar opens.
  • Use the official channel. Book through the restaurant’s website or the platform it links to, such as Tock, Resy, OpenTable or SevenRooms. Resold reservations are often against the restaurant’s terms and can be cancelled.
  • Join the waitlist. Cancellations happen, especially a day or two before. Many restaurants run a waitlist through their booking platform and offer freed-up tables in order.
  • Expect a deposit or prepayment. Many three-star restaurants take a deposit or the full menu price when you book, with strict cancellation rules. Check what is refundable before you pay.
  • Try lunch. Where a three-star restaurant serves lunch, it is often easier to book and sometimes cheaper. Our destination pages show lunch prices wherever a restaurant offers one.
  • In Japan, use a concierge or agency. Many top Tokyo and Kyoto restaurants only take bookings by phone in Japanese, through a hotel concierge or through specialist booking agencies.

Prices vary widely between countries. The typical three-star dinner tasting menu costs {{price3}} per person before drinks and service, with most between {{range3}}; a wine pairing adds about {{wine3}}.

faq.q: What is the highest Michelin star rating?
faq.a: Three stars. Michelin describes three stars as its highest honor, and there is no four- or five-star level. Only {{n3}} restaurants in the world hold three stars.
